_readme: Every credential this weft offers as a SHARED connection, keyed by
service name; each service holds a LIST of entries (always a list,
even for one). Copy this file to `access-apps.json` (gitignored) and
fill in the values, or point WEFT_ACCESS_APPS_FILE at your own copy.
Every entry declares its `kind`:
kind "oauth_app": an app users sign into through the service's
consent screen. Carries a `label` (the name the connection list
shows) and a `covers` set: exactly the permission ids (from the
service's catalogue) this app asks for. Each app appears as its own
one-click option in the editor with its `covers` shown; permissions
are FIXED per app, the user picks an option rather than ticking.
Several apps per service let a cheap permission tier avoid a
provider's review process. Each app pins the provider addresses it
signs in against (auth_url, token_url), copied from the access
node's service recipe; a connect through a registered app only ever
talks to these. Register the callback URL the access node's connect
panel shows (<this weft's public base>/access/oauth/callback) as the
app's redirect URL, and re-register it whenever the public base
changes. Some providers (Slack) only accept https callback URLs.
An `events` block on an app makes weft RECEIVE that service's event
pushes through this app: it carries only the per-deployment secret
material (a signing secret, a public key, a push audience); which
verification runs and every path comes from the service's own recipe.
kind "api_key": the runtime's own key for a pasted-key service
(openrouter, elevenlabs, ...): what the 'use the runtime's key' door
hands out. At most one per service.
A service listed nowhere offers no shared door: users bring their own
credential (paste a key, register their own app).
Keys starting with _ are ignored.

slack._setup: api.slack.com/apps -> Create New App (From scratch) -> OAuth & Permissions: add the callback URL as a Redirect URL and add your bot scopes. Client ID/Secret are under Basic Information.
slack.label: Slack
slack._setup_events: For event triggers via pushes: under Event Subscriptions, enable events, set the Request URL to <your public weft>/events/slack/messages, subscribe the bot to message.channels, and copy the Signing Secret (Basic Information) here.

google._setup: console.cloud.google.com -> APIs & Services -> Credentials -> Create OAuth client ID (Web application), enable the Drive API, add the callback URL as an Authorized redirect URI.
google.label: Google Drive
google._setup_events: Drive watch channels are pushed straight to weft, but Google only pushes to DOMAINS VERIFIED in this app's console: verify your weft's public domain there first.

google._setup: The same console; a second client kept broad. Google classes drive.readonly as restricted (review + audit), which is exactly why it is a SEPARATE app: the narrow one above ships without review.
google.label: Google Drive (full read)
google._setup_events: Drive watch channels are pushed straight to weft, but Google only pushes to DOMAINS VERIFIED in this app's console: verify your weft's public domain there first.
